title: 03 — Synth, timbre and sound design · Established (1)
text:
**Starting points for timbre.** Sine for sub and body; saw and square when the sound needs harmonics to be heard
above the wall; filters, envelopes, distortion, resonance and automation then fit it to the sub-genre
(`inbox/AICORE-flat/03-formas-onda-e-sintese.md`,
`05-aplicacao-psytrance.md:26-28`). On W-Core this is each
layer's wave and **Shape** knob (named shapes).

**One patch, two articulations.** The hi-tech recipe starts from a square wave with a simple arpeggio and adds a
triangle oscillator modulating the phase for a more robotic timbre; the pluck is the same timbre with a different
articulation, and the variation only touches some arpeggio steps
(`BEEP-E-PLUCK-HI-TECH.md`; in English in
technique cards). It is a transcript of a session in another DAW's modular synth,
marked "candidate recipe to try", with the parameter values to confirm.

**One sound per role in the templates.** Every Core-only template gives each role one Core instrument: kick → the
engine kick, bass → a Sampler with Diogo's bass samples or a W-Core bass preset, hats/perc/crash → the engine hats, accents and impacts → the engine kick with a
pitch drop, leads, pads, drones and textures → W-Core · Wave (template pages).

**Psytrance bass at 145** (`online`, not approved): osc A saw + B saw at +12, mono without portamento, an amplitude
envelope without attack, full sustain and short release, LP at 180–260 Hz with 10–15 % resonance, drive 15–25 %,
a filter envelope with ~40 ms decay and 15–25 % depth (above 40 % it becomes acid), a 4–8-bar LFO on the cutoff at
5–8 % (`estilos/psytrance.md:31`). In Core: a W-Core bass preset (*Saw Roller*).

**Growl.** In Core it is the native **GROWL** device: three formants above `Body` that move in eighths (`Talk`) and
are pushed by `Grit`; below `Body` the sound stays clean (4th-order Linkwitz-Riley split)
(catalogue, core-main#110). Presets per style and a help window exist
(presets, help); it is not heard yet.

title: 03 — Synth, timbre and sound design · Established (2)
text:
**Texture from the lead itself (resampling).** Isolate an attack, render it to audio, load it in a sampler with the
**sample's original note** as root, make a short version with a defined attack and a long one with delay/reverb, and
never send the same tail through the same reverb again
(`RESAMPLING-PLUCK-PARA-ATMOSFERA.md`).
In Core: **Bounce / Resample** (core-main#142) and F-Core's *Print to sample*.

**Long one-shot.** A note or phrase rendered with enough tail, kept as a normal and a reversed version: the reversed
one announces an entry, the normal one answers. Check the original note before transposing, and lower **only the
tail** when it covers the kick, keeping the attack
(`ONE-SHOTS-LONGOS-DE-SYNTH.md`).
**Gap:** Core has no reverse effect yet (F-Core phase 2); reverse the rendered file outside Core.

**Recording and resampling.** The transcript chapters
`24-gravacao-e-resampling-de-synths.md` and
`10-sintetizadores-automacao-e-cpu.md` describe the path
in Ableton (freeze/flatten, routing, CPU). In Core the equivalent is Bounce / Resample and exporting the song or a
clip (*Save as sample (WAV)…*).

title: 03 — Synth, timbre and sound design · Role, not name — and what to automate
text:
Two transcript chapters work as rules, not as new techniques:

- **The synth's name is not the decision.** What you choose is the musical role and the patch's behaviour: melody,
  sequence, texture, emphasiser, effect
  (`10-sintetizadores-automacao-e-cpu.md:5`).
  That is the logic of Core's templates, which give **one sound per role**.
- **Automation is movement, not decoration.** The automated parameters seen are cutoff, decay, volume, stereo width
  and effect amount; and the speed of the change is part of the decision — a fast change can work better than a slow
  one, depending on the rhythm (`10:7-17`). In the
  templates, the bass, lead and texture filters are automated, plus the master sweep
  (`core-template.md:88-89`); each template page lists what is automated.
- **Keep three decisions apart** when asking the helper for anything: creative (which sound and which movement),
  technical (freeze, consolidate, route) and validation (check that the result is still the same and that the
  ducking works) (`10:32-38`).

**Melody** (`inbox/AICORE-flat/09-melodias-e-arranjo.md`):
start simple, because it is easier to judge; choose the **octave by how it fits** with kick and bass, not by habit;
give the sequence movement with gradual changes of cutoff, decay, pitch, rhythm or density; **duplicate a section and
change the second half** instead of writing another idea, to avoid static repetition; and always listen **in the
track, never solo** (`09:18-24`). The templates do this by design: the lead comes in as call and response, and
Randomize varies grammar, gate, hats and roles per section from a seed.

The chapter's declared limit (`09:26-28`) still holds: the collection has no universal rules on key, scales or
melody. P-Core has 17 scales and arpeggios (patterns), marked as hypotheses, and no
Core track has been heard.

title: 03 — Synth, timbre and sound design · The "bubbly" sweep: function first, timbre later
text:
`22-sound-design-sweep-bubbly.md` describes making the
hi-tech signature synth once kick, bass and drums are done:

- set up the music before the timbre: make a MIDI region, use **G as the project's root note**, hold the note for the
  whole phrase, and design the sound in a modular instrument (`22:7-14`).
- the evolution comes from **continuous oscillator modulation**, texture and processing — not from a melody with
  several notes, because the note is long (`22:16-18`).
- the sound can serve five functions: transition, sweep, background texture, link between sections, hi-tech
  signature. **First find the function in the arrangement**, only then design the timbre (`22:20-30`).

`23-modulacao-e-stereo-em-sintese.md` opens how that
movement is made:

- **a slow, strong LFO on the pitch**, through a mixer, low Hz, high amount, bipolar, with polarity control: the main
  sweep (`23:3-12`). In Core, the track's **Modulation** (LFO, ENV and STEP tabs; core-main#139).
- **a second, faster and subtler LFO** for texture. Keeping macro and micro apart is what stops one LFO from doing
  both badly (`23:14-23`).
- the oscillator choice (triangle against one with more bite) is **by ear** (`23:25-27`).
- stereo by **phase offset**: different modulation on each side turns a mono source into a wide image (`23:29-31`).
  The four cautions: check mono compatibility, never widen the low end, check that the L/R difference does not cancel,
  and widen according to the sound's role and place (`23:33-38`).

The last caution is Diogo's bass rule: never a widener or Haas on the bass, low end mono
(`estilos/geral.md:41`). In Core: BODY widens only above the
sub, and Utility's *Mono below* keeps the low end in the middle. Above ~200 BPM the bass wave may not even finish a
cycle between notes (`estilos/hitech.md:69`).

title: 03 — Synth, timbre and sound design · Still open
text:
- None of the sound design has been heard: the R04 procedures have **zero A/B**
  (`R04/findings.md:25-30`).
- W-Core · Wave (leads, pads, drones, granular) is only a design (core-main#121).
- RISE is planned; reverse, tape stop and convolution are gaps.

title: 04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · Established (1)
text:
**The templates' shape.** Every template has 6 sections and 16-bar phrases; what changes is the length and the
energy per section. The Core-only templates keep these numbers (template pages).

| Style | Bars | Sections (energy) |
|---|---|---|
| Dark psycore | 384 | Intro 32 (1), Groove 64 (3), Development 96 (4), Break 32 (0), Return 96 (4), Outro 64 (2) (`estilos/darkpsycore.md:27`) |
| Hi-tech | 320 | Intro 32 (1), Groove 64 (3), Development 64 (4), Break 32 (0), Main 96 (4), Outro 32 (2) (`estilos/hitech.md:27`) |
| Slambient | 320 | Intro 32 (1), Layers 64 (2), Transform 64 (3), Reduction 32 (1), Deep 96 (3), Outro 32 (1) (`estilos/slambient.md:26`) |
| Darkpsy / Twilight / Progressive | 288 | Intro 32, Groove 64, Development 64, Break 32, Return (or Main) 64, Outro 32 (`core-template.md:64-72`) |
| Full-on | 272 | Intro 32, Groove 32, Development 64, Break 48, Return 64, Outro 32 (`core-template.md:71`) |

All `codigo`: what is in the files, not what was approved by ear.

**Rules repeated in every style** (`core-template.md:82-89`):

- Track roles: kick, bass (KBBB family), closed hats, open hats, percussion, accents, lead in call and response (not in
  slambient), texture, atmosphere, impacts and risers.
- Each section has an energy level that decides what plays.
- A fill in the last bar of each 16-bar phrase; one bar without kick before each lift; a riser (an accelerating roll)
  and a master high-pass sweep into it; an impact on the first beat.
- The fall into Break/Reduction is marked the same way: one bar without kick or hats before it, an impact on the
  first beat, and energy down by 2 or more.
- No track has two clips playing at once (the tests check it). Bass, lead and texture filters automated; a fade at the end.
- Master sweep: up to 900 Hz in hi-tech (`hitech.md:29`),
  up to 400 Hz in slambient (`slambient.md:29`).
  Riser: a geometric ramp of 2→48 notes over 4 bars in hi-tech; 8 bars (2→24) in slambient.

title: 04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · Established (2)
text:
In Core the risers, sweeps and impacts are **F-Core** intents (*Build-up*, *Impact*, *Downlifter*), and the reverb and
delay that follow the sections are **R-Core** and **D-Core**. **S-Core · Stages** (planned) will apply all of them per
section with named presets (how plugins work).

**Slambient has no drops.** Layers instead of drops
(`estilos/slambient.md:27`); drone up to energy 3,
granular texture from energy 2.

**Tempo policy** (`decisao_diogo`): a section leaves the style's range only if it is short (< 1/4 of the song) and
within ±40 % of the BPM, with a warning; the first and last sections stay at the song's BPM, so a DJ can mix in and out
(`estilos/geral.md:7`).

**Contrast as a decision rule.** The chapters
`25-contraste-e-impacto.md`,
`26-transicao-e-tensao.md` and
`27-contraste-como-regra-de-arranjo.md` sort the kinds of
contrast (density, register, space, rhythm) and the choice model. The thesis: a section's energy is only felt as the
difference from the previous one, and the change must be audible in one thing at a time.

**Phrases and long listening** (`externo`): in psytrance, change something every 32 bars, leads and rhythms every 8,
layers every 4–8, tracks between 6 and 10 minutes
(`estilos/psytrance.md:20`).

title: 04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · The transcript's method: one block, then subtraction
text:
`12-arranjo-e-fluxo.md` records the process seen, and it is the opposite
of "writing sections one after another":

- start from **one 32-bar section** and repeat it to the target length — six or seven minutes (`12:5`).
- the **intro is made by removal**: take synths, kick, bass, high hats and percussion out of the first block, leaving
  less density to bring elements in gradually (`12:7-18`).
- the arrangement is an **energy flow**: progressive entries, temporary removals, density changes, preparation before
  an element comes in, contrast between full and empty sections (`12:20-28`).
- to decide, each section is a **set of active elements**
  (`section: intro / kick: absent or later / bass: absent / melodies: very reduced / percussion: minimal /
  goal: make space and prepare the entry`), compared with the full block (`12:30-43`).

Core already does this: the templates have energy per section and **the energy level decides what plays**
(`core-template.md:82-88`); Randomize moves the lead entry to ¼ or
½ of the section, and percussion/accents/open hats come and go only at energy ≥ 3, never leaving the energy-4 section
(`core-randomize.md`, axis `E`). What chapter 12 did **not**
describe — break structure, build-up, drop, how long each element stays (`12:45-47`) — is now the section table in
styles.

title: 04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · Metre, phrase and the rule that is not a rule
text:
`13-tempo-compasso-e-frases.md`: the timeline is divided by a grid
that zooms but keeps regular divisions; BPM is beats per minute; in 4/4 the kick marks each beat; **a phrase is 8 bars
(32 beats)**, and changes — a crash or a new element — mark the start of a phrase; several phrases make a section
(intro, build-up, drop, break, outro) (`13:5-21`). The key line: **8 and 32 bars are reference points, not
compulsory rules** (`13:32`).

The four things the transcript requires before suggesting an entry or a removal (`13:25-30`) are the four Core's
`get_context` returns: BPM, time signature, on which beat/bar/phrase the change is, and whether the change confirms or
breaks the expectation.

title: 04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · The energy curve and the five contrasts
text:
`14-dinamica-e-historia-musical.md`: interest does not come
from adding elements, it comes from **removing information at strategic moments**. The curve is built with progressive
entry; filters on kick and bass during the build-up; more percussion, leads and layers; drops with full kick and bass;
breaks with drastic reduction; removing snare, FM leads or percussion to create tension; elements of the intro coming
back in the break or outro; and a final filter on kick and bass to close (`14:8-18`).

Contrast can be **rhythmic, spectral, harmonic, timbral or of density** (`14:20-22`). One explicit technique, flagged
as not a law: **delay the main drop by one bar** after a long build-up for more tension (`14:24-28`).

The narrative seen, section by section (`14:30-41`): intro with sub-bass and ambience → build-up with more high-tech
and filters → drop 1 with strong kick and bass and few layers → development with arpeggio, melodies, drums, leads and
percussion → break with less energy and the ambience back → final drop with more density → deconstruction by gradual
removal → outro with kick and bass filtered to the end. The record asked per section (`14:43-54`) has eight fields:
expected energy, active elements, removed elements, planned change, transition mechanism, narrative function, length
in bars, and contrast with the previous and next sections.

title: 04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · Visual planning, symmetry and surprise
text:
`15-marcadores-e-automacao-de-energia.md`: the producer
splits the timeline into sections and uses helper tracks to mark phrases and see the energy **before detailed
listening** (`15:3-5`). In Core these are the ruler's named sections (each with its colour) plus the energy level the
templates already carry.

The rule of measure: repeating similar lengths helps the listener predict the form, but varying the number of phrases
or a section's length stops the arrangement from sounding mechanical — balance expectation and surprise (`15:22-24`).
In Randomize this is axis `G` (section lengths and the 8-bar phrase), **not done yet**
(`core-randomize.md` §Not yet).

title: 04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · Where it is
04 — Arrangement, energy and contrast · Still open
text:
- Section lengths and the 8-bar phrase are Randomize's axis `G`, not done yet.
- Effects and automation per variation (axes `H`–`I`), same.
- No Core track has been heard from start to end: the structures come from the generated templates, not from listening.
- S-Core · Stages, which will make the sections a plugin, is planned.

title: 05 — Mix and master · Established (1)
text:
**Diogo's four rules** (`decisao_diogo`, the only mix rules that are law):

- Hats and open hats always ≥ 8–10 dB below the kick's peak; never raise hats to fill bands
  (`estilos/geral.md:38`).
- The bass goes up in small steps: ≤ +3 dB per version, measured on the 16th grid (`geral.md:39`).
- Never a widener or Haas on the bass; the low end is mono (`geral.md:41`).
- The master does not redo the mix: a kick 2–3 dB above the bass is fixed in the mix (`geral.md:60`).

**Approved levels per style** (`decisao_diogo`, trim in dB with faders at 0, approved 2026-11-04):

| Role | Hi-tech (`hitech.md:66`) | Dark psycore (`darkpsycore.md:70`) |
|---|---|---|
| kick | 0 | 0 |
| bass | +9 | +9 |
| hats | −22.8 | −32.7 |
| open-hats | −15 | −22.8 |
| perc | −15.8 | −10 |
| accents | −27 | −27 |
| lead | −10.5 | −10.8 |
| texture | −15 | −15 |
| atmos | −11 | −11 |
| impact | −6 | −6 |
| riser | −10 | −10 |

Slambient and psytrance have no approved levels (slambient only `estudo`; psytrance nothing).

**Sampler level per role** (`codigo`): the loudest 100 ms of the sample go to the role's target — kick −9, bass −11,
hats −19, perc −17, accents −15, impact −13, riser −17, no role −16 dBFS; between −24 and +24 dB, never more than
6 dB above full scale (`core-samples.md:107-110`,
`estilos/geral.md:42`).

**Master targets:**

| Destination | LUFS | True peak | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre-master | peak −6 to −3 dBFS without limiter, crest 10–16 dB, up to 6 stem groups | — | `externo` (`geral.md:51`) |
| Streaming | −11 integrated (range −12 to −9), crest 7–11 | −1.0 dBTP (Core ceiling −1.4) | `decisao_diogo` (`geral.md:52`) |
| Club | −7 integrated (range −8 to −6), crest 5–8 | −0.3 dBTP (Core ceiling −0.8) | `estudo`; measured ~−7.5 LUFS on the PC, left for later (`geral.md:53`) |

title: 05 — Mix and master · Established (2)
text:
Approved and measured masters: hi-tech −10.9 and −11.7 LUFS, dark psycore −11.0, both at −1.26 dBTP
(`R05/findings.md:93-96`). Approved chains:
hi-tech with utility drive +12 dB, preset utility +4.9 dB, HP 38 Hz, notch 200 Hz and a 2nd EQ at −2.5 dB at
3.2 kHz Q4 (the squelch band); dark psycore with drive +8.58 dB, HP 30 Hz and notch 240 Hz
(`hitech.md:74`,
`darkpsycore.md:76`). All of it is done with
Core's engine effects (`eq`, `compressor`, `utility`, `saturation`, `limiter`).

**What each Core-only template sets on its master** (compressor, utility gain, limiter ceiling) is in the
template pages. Those are config values; no LUFS has been measured for the
Core-only templates yet.

**Chain order** (`codigo`, `geral.md:54`): high-pass (carries the riser sweep) → drive (gain before the EQ) →
corrective EQ (shelf at the kick fundamental, notch at the bass root's harmonic, air) → glue compression → on
hi-tech, 2nd EQ in the squelch band → stereo image → saturation → limiter last. The master's `gainDb` only goes up
to +12; the rest of the drive goes to the preset's utility (`geral.md:56`). Releases: compressor 0.25–0.5 of the
beat, limiter ≤ 0.35 of the beat at the fastest BPM (`geral.md:59`).

**Mud.** 150–300 Hz: HP on pads and FX at 300–500 Hz, reverb returns at 400–600 Hz, a 1–2 dB dip around 200 Hz on
the bass; to find it, sweep a 6 dB boost with Q ~3 between 150–300 Hz on the bus. Measured on Core's original
template: mud at 120–300 Hz and 5–8 dB less between 300 Hz and 16 kHz than the references
(`estilos/geral.md:46`,
`R05/findings.md`). In Core, R-Core · Reverb
already high-passes its returns per preset (presets.md).

**Measured references** (`medido`): hi-tech at 175 → −7.4 LUFS, +1.3 dBTP, crest 9.7; psycore at 190 → −10.5 LUFS,
0.8 dBTP, crest 12.0 (`dados/masterizacao.json`).

title: 05 — Mix and master · Order and intent in a track's chain
text:
`inbox/AICORE-flat/11-processamento-de-melodias-e-synths.md`
transcribes chains on melodies and synths. The only thing there that is a **rule with a reason** is the order:

- the **delay goes after the compressor**, so the compressor does not squash the delay's repeats — the goal is to
  keep the note's attack while the effect goes on (`11:15-17`). The approved templates do it: hi-tech has
  `delay 0.375 ping-pong` on the lead track and dark psycore has `HP 200 + delay 0.75 ping-pong` on the Acid, with
  the **bass** chain's compressor before the mono utility
  (`estilos/hitech.md:48`,
  `estilos/darkpsycore.md:50`). In Core the
  delay is D-Core · Delay or ECHO.
- the intents seen: cut unneeded low end; cut a problem region (built-up mids); compress to **bring out or catch the
  first transient** (PUNCH does this for kick and bass); saturate for presence and density (BODY, `saturation`);
  a **short** reverb for space (SPACE, R-Core); widening **with care**; set the level of whooshes and tails by hand;
  consolidate several elements before processing further (`11:19-28`).
- the five-question decision model: what is missing or too much, which tool fixes it, does the effect act before or
  after the others, what risk it brings (clash, noise, too much width, lost transient), and how to check it (listen
  in context, look at the spectrum, test mono when needed) (`11:30-38`).

**Five things the transcription refuses to make a rule** (`11:40-45`): do not always cut the same frequency; do not
always widen; do not compress to hit a fixed value; do not put delay and reverb in one order for every sound; do not
freeze a track before the patch and the automation are right.

Where this clashes with Diogo's decisions, Diogo wins: widening is "with care" on synths, but **a widener or Haas
on the bass is forbidden, and the low end is mono** (`decisao_diogo`,
`estilos/geral.md:41`). For consolidating, Core now has
Bounce / Resample (round 4, core-main#142); see 13 — Engine and limits.

title: 05 — Mix and master · Where it is
text:
`dados/masterizacao.json` (targets, order, per
style, engine state M-1…M-6) and
`dados/mastering-presets.json` (the 7
chains, parameter by parameter); `inbox/core-improvements/conhecimento/research/R05/` (4-level diagnosis,
measuring protocol, what the meter does);
`inbox/AICORE-flat/07-master-e-low-end.md`.

title: 05 — Mix and master · Still open
text:
- **Gap: EQ below 200 Hz.** The engine `eq`'s `midFreq` starts at 200 Hz, so the classic 150 Hz dip cannot be
  reached (M-2, `geral.md:86`). Core has no equivalent yet.
- Fixing in the master is a mistake: the diagnosis goes down level by level to the track
  (`R05/findings.md:15-22`). Not yet applied to
  real cases.
- There is no complete before/after case in the whole collection — problem, decision, measures, listening
  (`R05/gaps.md:9`).
- Core's meter follows BS.1770-4 at 0.1 LU resolution with 4× true peak, but **there is no LRA** and no loudness
  readout on the app surface (M-G1, M-G2).
- The club target and a slambient master are not approved; the Core-only templates have no measured LUFS.

title: 08 — Style templates and how they are made
text:
# 08 — Style templates and how they are made

A template (`core-template`) is a whole song — BPM, sections, tracks with instrument and values, patterns placed as
clips, effect chains, mix and automation — wrapped with `id`, `style`, `version` and `description`. It is the
starting point, not the result.

**Every template, track by track, with every effect and value and the master chain, is in
plugins/templates/.** That page is generated from the template files, so it is
always what Core loads.

title: 08 — Style templates and how they are made · Established (1)
text:
**What a template is and is not.** The pattern (rhythm) and the instrument (sound) stay apart: changing the sound
does not change the rhythm. A template carries no audio. `id` is `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,40}` and equals the file name;
`version` goes up each time it is saved; `source.kind` is `builtin`, `user` or `analysis` (song → template, written
by AICORE, read-only for Core) (`core-template.md:24-36`). A
song made from it keeps `template: {id, version, style}` — and it is the `style` that guides the sample suggestions.

In the window: *Library > Templates* lists the templates grouped by style; **File > Save as template** saves the
current song as your template, and *Delete template* / *Restore built-in templates* hide and show the app's
(`core-template.md` §In the window).

**Where they live.** `templates/` next to `Core.exe` (read-only, copied from the repository) and
`%APPDATA%\Core\Templates` (yours). A template of yours with the same `id` takes the app's place in the menu without
touching the app's file; *Delete template* hides the app's one in `hidden.json`.

**Core only (`decisao_diogo`, 2026-11-05).** Templates use only Core's own instruments and effects (Core has no VST) and no
loaded samples.

**In the app** (core-main#177, #183, #244, #247, `decisao_diogo`): only the templates made from Diogo's references are
listed: `hitech-ref` (190 BPM, from Wake Up and Remember), `slambient-ref` (250 BPM, from The Well and Ketamine),
`slambient-deep` (200 BPM), `psycore-tremolo` (210 BPM, from the Inferi tab) and `psycore-blacktide` (210 BPM, from
Black Tide). All sit at about −17 LUFS on purpose. The 16 older templates carry `"source": {"kind": "builtin", "base":
true}`: they stay in `templates/` as bases for the generators and tests, and the Library hides them. Their pages are
marked "base, not in the app".

The 16 older templates (core-main round 4, `e0a05aa`) have 6–11 tracks, 6 sections, ppq 960, 4/4:

title: 08 — Style templates and how they are made · Established (2)
text:
| Style | Templates (`id`) | BPM | Bars |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dark psycore | `darkpsycore-minimal`, `darkpsycore`, `darkpsycore-dense`, `darkpsycore-syncopated` | 210, 225, 240, 255 | 384 |
| Hi-tech | `hitech-minimal`, `hitech`, `hitech-dense`, `hitech-triplets` | 175, 190, 205, 220 | 320 |
| Slambient | `slambient-minimal`, `slambient`, `slambient-dense`, `slambient-extreme` | 240, 300, 360, 450 | 320 |
| Psytrance | `darkpsy`, `twilight`, `fullon`, `progressive` | 155, 148, 146, 138 | 288 / 288 / 272 / 288 |

The `name` inside the files says *spaced*, *clean* and *deep* where the `id` says `-minimal` — two vocabularies for
the same thing; the manual uses the `id`. The BPM ranges per style are `decisao_diogo`
(`core-template.md:64-72`).

**What each variant does** (measured on the old files, INVENTARIO §5; the Core-only files keep the same
structure): the section structure is identical within a style — BPM and tracks change.

- `-minimal` drops 2 tracks (*Percussion* and *Accents*) and lowers density by ~1 note per bar.
- `-dense` adds no tracks: BPM goes up (+15/+15/+60) and so do the notes, mostly in *Percussion* and the leads.
- `-syncopated` (+30 BPM) has **fewer** notes: the K-B-B with a rest thins *Bass* and *Bass growl*.
- `-triplets` (+30) puts about 27 % of its notes off the 1/16 grid and 36 % on the triplet grid (tick % 320) — that
  is how a triplet is told apart mechanically.
- `-extreme` (+150 BPM in slambient) cuts bass notes and lasts under 3 minutes.

**How they are made.** By `tools/templates/make_templates.py` with `arrange.py`, `levels.py`, `realtrack.py` and
`calibrate.py`. Once generated, **the files are the source** and are edited like any template
(`core-template.md:62`). Calibration renders each template on the PC, sets each track's level against the kick by the
approved dark psycore balance, and sets the master drive so the main part gives −11 LUFS with the approved streaming
chain (true peak ≤ −1 dBTP). For the Core-only templates this calibration has **not been re-run and measured** yet.

title: 08 — Style templates and how they are made · Established (3)
text:
**What the tests guarantee:** each template is read, saved back the same, accepted by the engine; the BPM is in the
style's range; and 4 bars around the main section do not pass 0 dBFS.

text:
core-main `templates/`, `docs/contracts/core-template.md`, `tools/templates/`; this manual's copies in
`plugins/data/templates/` and pages in `plugins/templates/`;
the source of the choices is `inbox/AICORE/docs/knowledge/core-styles-source-inventory.json` and
`inbox/core-improvements/conhecimento/dados/online.json` (17 substyles, 29 findings, 15 sources).

text:

- Leads, pads and drones in the templates use the simple engine `bass` instrument with effects: **gap** until
  W-Core · Wave exists.
- There is no template of Diogo's saved from a song of his (`source.kind: user`). Song → template
  (`source.kind: analysis`) is AICORE's job (AICORE#37, core-main#117).
- No template uses S-Core · Stages yet (planned): sections are built by the template generator, not by a plugin.

title: 09 — Patterns, P-Core and Randomize
text:
# 09 — Patterns, P-Core and Randomize

Three ways to put notes on a track, with different amounts of control. Knowing which to use is half the work of a
style.

title: 09 — Patterns, P-Core and Randomize · Established (1)
text:
**1. Write by hand.** Pattern editor: step grid for drums, note editor for the bass; pattern length 1–16 bars; grid
1/32 to 1/4; play live on the editor's track (keys Z S X D C V G B H N J M , or a MIDI keyboard) — but notes played
live are **not** recorded into the pattern; MIDI recording does not exist yet
(`app/README.md` §Current limits).

**2. Randomize within the style** (`codigo`,
`core-randomize.md`). Only works on songs made from a template.
Axes A–F by default, J and K only when asked:

title: 09 — Patterns, P-Core and Randomize · Established (2)
text:
| Axis | What it varies |
|---|---|
| A `bass` | Grammar per section (energy ≥ 2) and turns. Menus per style: dark `kbbb, kbb, kb-b`; hi-tech `kbbb, kbb, triplet`; slambient `kbb, kbbb, offbeat`; darkpsy/twilight `kbbb, kbb, kb-b`; full-on `kbbb` (turns with fifths and octaves), `kbb`; progressive `kbb, kbbb, offbeat` |
| B `gate` | Bass note length: a fraction of the gap and **never more than the style's ms** (dark 0.5–0.6 / 32–45 ms; hi-tech 0.55–0.6 / 40–50; slambient 0.55–0.7 / 25–45; darkpsy 35–50; twilight 45–60; full-on 50–65; progressive 55–75) |
| C `hats` | Closed-hat grid and 1/32 rolls |
| D `kick` | Ghost kick on the last 16th, only with energy ≥ 3 |
| E `roles` | Percussion, accents and open hats come in/out (energy ≥ 3; energy 4 never loses them); lead entry at ¼ or ½ of the section |
| F `fills` | Fills every 8 or 16 bars; 1–2 bars without kick/bass/hats before a rise or a drop; riser of 2, 4 or 8 bars ending on the drop |
| J `tempo` | BPM per section in steps: slower in the break, back or faster in the drop; first and last at the song's BPM; outside the style's range only for a short section ( Randomize
  (Shuffle, Random pitches, Humanize more) also skips states already seen and says when every one has been shown.
- **Align** (core-main#184, `codigo`, values are hypotheses until heard): a row in step 1 and a button next to
  Write/Again. It keeps the notes and only lines up the kick, the bass, the hats and the cymbals, in one Ctrl+Z.
  Seven ways, one per style (`aligns` in `styles.json`; each style has its `align`): fullon, progressive (no bass on
  the 1/16 after the kick), darkpsy, psycore, hitech, slambient, twilight. Rules: kick and bass never together; the
  bass stops `bassTailMs` before the next kick; the first bass after a kick is softer (80/100/100); hats softer on
  the kick, offbeat on top, with the style's swing/push; the grid is detected (triplets stay); Align twice = Align
  once. The kick comes from the selected kick track, else the song's kick track (only read), else every beat; it is
  found in song time over every repetition of every clip (core-main#190).
- Names: menus and lists say **Patterns**; the open window keeps the title P-Core (Diogo, 2026-11-07: the X-Core
  names make the plugins easy to explain to the AI).
- Tested in two audits (2026-11-07, core-main#190 and #192): see what changed.
- As a function: `PCore(style, section, role, …) -> Pattern`; its call for the AI bridge is specified but not
  registered yet (how plugins work).

title: 09 — Patterns, P-Core and Randomize · Established (3)
text:
**The pattern library** (`core-pattern`): a pattern is only notes (tick, length, pitch, velocity) with a name, role
and styles to find it; **any pattern works on any track** — role and styles only sort and filter. The names are the
files' `name`, as the window shows them; the full list per folder is in patterns.md.
The bass patterns are the same material as the 12 constructions of
`bass-variation-examples.json` — see
02 kick and bass. Vocabulary note: the DnB breaks and the rides come from families that **are
not psytrance**; they are there as break material, and using them in a style is Diogo's call.

title: 09 — Patterns, P-Core and Randomize · Where it is
text:
core-main `docs/contracts/core-randomize.md` and `docs/contracts/core-pcore.md`; this manual's copy of the P-Core data
in `plugins/data/pcore/`; KBBB and elastic bass
§E1–E5 (the five elasticity recipes, always with a fixed kick and compensated level);
`inbox/core-improvements/_branches/conhecimento/pcore/2026-11-05-pcore-pattern-study.md` (31 patterns, 1255 notes,
all `hypothesis`).

title: 09 — Patterns, P-Core and Randomize · Still open
text:
- The P-Core study says its patterns are synthetic notes, not transcriptions; no track has been heard; there is no
  statistical corpus per genre. It separates what is read evidence (builds 8/16/32; roll 2–4 bars,
  1/8→1/16→1/32) from editorial choice (crescendo 0.35→0.85, a 12-semitone rise, one beat of silence).
- `styles.json` needs Diogo's choices; the patterns need listening.
- Axes G (section length, 8-bar phrase), H–I (effects and automation) and sound per section do not exist. S-Core ·
  Stages (planned) will place P-Core per section.

title: 10 — Production workflow: from the starting point to the WAV
text: # 10 — Production workflow: from the starting point to the WAV

title: 10 — Production workflow: from the starting point to the WAV · The base path, in today's Core (1)
text:
1. **Library > Templates** — pick a style and BPM. Core lists the 5 templates made from Diogo's references (the 16 older ones are bases, not shown)
   (08 — Style templates, template pages). The song is
   born with sections, track roles, energy, automation and mix already in place, all with Core's own plugins.
2. **Shape the sounds with Core plugins** — the Sampler with Diogo's samples or a W-Core bass preset for the bass, the devices (GROWL, METAL, PUNCH, ZAP, BODY…)
   per role, F-Core · FX for an intent, R-Core / D-Core for space and echo per section. Which plugin fits which style:
   styles; every preset with its values: presets.
3. **Samples, if you want them** — *Samples > Suggest samples…* fills the tracks in **one Undo step**; *Shuffle
   samples* varies (seed), *Use the best samples* fixes the best choice. The level goes to the role's target. See
   07 — Samples and the sample database.
4. **Listen to the kick/bass pair at the real BPM** and fix the articulation before adding layers
   (`28-percursos-de-producao.md`).
5. **Vary within the style** with *Edit > Randomize* (subtle/medium/bold) or by writing patterns with P-Core
   (09 — Patterns).
6. **A starting point per style**, picking the right cards (technique cards):

title: 10 — Production workflow: from the starting point to the WAV · The base path, in today's Core (2)
text:
| Style | Work path |
|---|---|
| Hi-tech | base (kick + bass, then hats/shaker/fills) → timbre (beep and pluck from the same patch, or an FM lead — **gap** until W-Core · Wave) → arrangement (intro, layers in stages, a readable motif; if the drop loses impact, delay or lower a secondary layer) |
| Psytrance | base (kick/bass relation; percussion with accents) → motif (the lead's attack as anticipation; confirm the WAV's root note) → substyle (full-on, twilight, progressive have their own profiles and templates) |
| Dark | darkpsy (a sustained dark texture + a lead up front; formant/resonance/slow modulation: GROWL, Core FX Modulate) · dark psycore (a glitch fill with the lead's attack: GLITCH; metallic body in the mids protecting the sub: METAL, BODY) · dark hi-tech (KBBB, a tension pause, ambience/lead contrast, a dialogue of timbres) · slambient (turn an attack into a long texture: F-Core Atmosphere, SPACE; let the tail fall back before the bass returns) |

   Each path ends with **what to listen for**: "the pulse holds and every answer has room", "the fill has a job in
   the phrase, ends in time and keeps the groove".
7. **Leave the loop for the timeline**: take the whole track, save, close, reopen, export and compare with what you
   hear in the project, using a stretch as a musical regression test
   (`roadmap/2026-11-03-plano-producao-pessoal.md`).
8. **Export**: *File > Export WAV 24-bit / 32-bit float*, whole song + 2 s of tail, no normalisation, in the
   background. Bounce / Resample of a track or region is in round 4 (core-main#142); stems in the window do not exist
   yet.

title: 10 — Production workflow: from the starting point to the WAV · What the personal plan calls "done"
text:
The milestone is to make a track of his own from the first loop to the final WAV, come back to the project later and
**repeat the same decisions**. Hence the practices repeated across the collection:

- Always work on a **copy** of the template for each sound experiment.
- One A/B at a time: the same eight bars, three versions (original; reference kick in the same place; reference kick
  with the bass rebalanced), keeping every other parameter. Diogo does not A/B presets one by one: presets are
  checked by an automated render-and-measure sweep (core-main#124: 80 presets, 0 failures).
- Add saturation, compressor and limiter **one at a time**, with compensated levels for comparison.
- Note the operations that repeat — that is what shows what the interface lacks.
- Make a **personal template** with your own sounds, levels and routes, with clear names for the variants.

The step-by-step procedures are in
`dados/procedimentos.json` (10 sequences: pick a
style, pick samples, set levels, try a plugin in A/B, change the tempo in a section, new song, streaming master, drop
into a break…) and in `estilos/geral.md:200-204`.

title: 14 — From the first idea to a track in Core
text:
# 14 — From the first idea to a track in Core

A practical path to try arrangement, harmony and sound design. The values in the table describe files shipped with
Core. The exercises are work proposals to compare by ear.

title: 14 — From the first idea to a track in Core · 1. Pick a starting point
text:
Open **Library > Templates** (Ctrl+Shift+N by default) and pick a template per style. **File > New** opens an empty
song. With the sample library indexed, the **Samples** menu can suggest sounds, pick the best options or try another
pick with **Shuffle samples (another good pick)**. App guide.

| Template | Starting BPM | Bars and structure |
|---|---:|---|
| Dark Psycore | 225 | 384 · Intro 32 → Groove 64 → Development 96 → Break 32 → Return 96 → Outro 64 |
| Hi-Tech | 190 | 320 · Intro 32 → Groove 64 → Development 64 → Break 32 → Main 96 → Outro 32 |
| Slambient | 300 | 320 · Intro 32 → Layers 64 → Transform 64 → Reduction 32 → Deep 96 → Outro 32 |
| Full-on | 146 | 272 · Intro 32 → Groove 32 → Development 64 → Break 48 → Return 64 → Outro 32 |
| Progressive psy | 138 | 288 · Intro 32 → Groove 64 → Development 64 → Break 32 → Main 64 → Outro 32 |
| Twilight / Darkpsy | 148 / 155 | 288 · Intro 32 → Groove 64 → Development 64 → Break 32 → Return 64 → Outro 32 |

The first three last about 6:50, 6:44 and 4:16 at constant BPM in 4/4; tempo automation changes that. Every track,
effect and value of each template: template pages.

title: 14 — From the first idea to a track in Core · 2. Build eight bars
text:
1. Solo kick and bass at the real BPM. In **P-Core · Patterns**, pick the style, root and shape of the track. KBBB
   fills a beat with a kick on the first sixteenth and three bass notes on the others. Try one variation of accent,
   gate or octave at a time.
2. On the bass (a W-Core bass preset or the Sampler), compare a preset with a version with shorter notes (gate and
   `env1Decay`). In 4/4 a sixteenth lasts 66.7 ms
   at 225 BPM, 78.9 ms at 190 and 50 ms at 300. Listen to the kick's tail, the bass length and the phase at the attack.
   Gate, audible envelope and sidechain measure or change different things.
3. Add hats and percussion. Compare their peaks with the kick at the same metering point. The fader trim in dB is an
   adjustment and is not the track's peak.
4. Duplicate the block and change one element only: an octave answer, a fill at the phrase end or a shorter delay
   tail. Keep the original to compare. Kick and bass ·
   Synthetic bass examples.

title: 14 — From the first idea to a track in Core · 3. Make movement with rhythm, timbre and harmony
text:
A held tonic helps judge the groove and hear timbre changes. The bass note can change and stay mono. P-Core offers
scales to try; the roots and modes of a template belong to that example.

- **Dark Psycore.** Repeat the pedal and try **GROWL** on the last bass note of the KBBB, the beat's fourth step.
  Compare with growl on the second bass note and with the dry block. For melodic tension, try a short answer over
  the pedal, heard in context.
- **Hi-Tech.** Compare the same motif in two octaves, or alternate a sixteenth phrase with a triplet answer. Keep the
  change to one phrase to judge the articulation.
- **Slambient.** Keep the kick soft and try bringing in or taking out a drone or a texture (F-Core · FX *Atmosphere*,
  SPACE). Use space and register to tell sections apart while keeping the character with no lead.
- **Full-on, Twilight and Progressive.** A lead, pluck or arp can carry the harmonic change (**gap**: Core's lead
  synth W-Core · Wave is planned; today use the engine `bass` instrument with effects). Try the bass on a pedal first,
  then a version that follows the harmony. A progression like Am–G–F is an exercise, with bass and kick checked for
  every note.

Scale, interval and where the growl sits are choices judged by listening. Synth and sound design ·
Styles.

title: 14 — From the first idea to a track in Core · 4. Shape the track and pick FX
text:
Start from the section where the groove works. Make an intro by subtraction, make contrast in the middle and prepare
the way out. Try bringing a layer in or out in blocks of 8 or 16 bars. For a transition, compare silence, a fill, a
riser or a reverse tail before combining them.

| Intent | Starting point (Core) | What to compare |
|---|---|---|
| Growl or metal in Dark Psycore | **GROWL** preset *KBBB talk* (knob **Talk**), or **METAL** tuned to the song's note | The answer's character and the separation from the kick |
| Hi-Tech accent | **ZAP** (lasers), or **GLITCH** (stutter) | A short variation in the fill and the attack's definition |
| Slambient depth | **SPACE** (haunted / huge), **R-Core · Reverb** per section | The tail inside the layers and the clarity of the sub |
| Psytrance movement | the engine `filter` on cutoff and resonance (acid), **Core FX** (*Twilight swirl*, *Tension phaser*) | The resonance peak, the level and the room between notes |
| Transition with a sample | **F-Core · FX**, choosing **Build-up**, **Impact** or **Atmosphere** | Dry against treated, at similar gain |

The style racks (`rack:darkpsycore/growl-talk`, `rack:hitech/zap-laser`, `rack:slambient/haunted`,
`rack:psytrance/acid-lead`…) put these together in one go and now play Core's native steps; their step lists are in
presets › style racks. Confirm values in the interface, keep peak
headroom, and compare before saving a preset. Catalogue.

title: 14 — From the first idea to a track in Core · 5. Check and export
text:
- [ ] Kick and bass keep the attack and room you want in the densest sections.
- [ ] Hats, percussion and accents keep their role without taking over the groove.
- [ ] The low end keeps its image when heard in mono.
- [ ] The most important transition works in context before and after the change.
- [ ] The export was heard and measured; loudness and true peak were compared with the target's reference.
- [ ] For each technique judged, keep template, BPM, bar, A/B versions, change, measurement and listening decision.
  Mix and master · Gaps.
